description: Original editing rules for retrieval-augmented planning. These are principles, not copied timelines or creator presets.

allowed: public metadata used as a research pointer
original editorial graphics whose generated nature is recorded
disallowed: claiming public videos were used for model fine-tuning without permission
fabricated gameplay, screenshots, quotes, results, people, or evidence
copying a creator's exact edit sequence or identity

minecraft_narrative.goal: Make changing game state and player stakes immediately legible.

gaming.goal: Keep action readable while using reactions and proof to reinforce the spoken story.

talking_head.goal: Preserve natural delivery while removing drag and visualizing only the ideas that benefit from proof or clarification.

general.goal: Prioritize clarity, emotional contrast, continuity, and honest sourcing.

rules.rule: Open on the clearest stake, contradiction, threat, or outcome the source actually supports.
rules.rationale: A specific unanswered question gives the viewer a reason to continue.
rules.guardrail: Do not promise an outcome absent from the transcript or footage.

rules.rule: Place visual changes on state changes: new goal, player, place, resource, danger, setback, or result.
rules.rationale: Cuts become meaningful when they track what changed.
rules.guardrail: Do not cut merely because a fixed number of seconds elapsed.

rules.rule: Preserve cause before consequence unless a deliberate cold-open reveal is later contextualized.
rules.rationale: Viewers should understand why the next event matters.
rules.guardrail: Avoid chronology changes that make claims misleading.

rules.rule: Give the payoff a readable shot and a short reaction window; do not bury it under another effect.
rules.rationale: Contrast and breathing room make the resolution land.
rules.guardrail: Do not manufacture a reaction or extend it deceptively.

rules.rule: Remove true filler, abandoned starts, dead air, and redundant clauses while preserving meaning and human cadence.
rules.rationale: Compression should increase information density without sounding robotic.
rules.guardrail: Words such as like, so, right, and okay are not fillers when semantically necessary.

rules.rule: Prefer sentence, clause, breath, or action boundaries for cuts; use short audio fades at discontinuities.
rules.rationale: Invisible audio continuity matters more than aggressive visual cutting.
rules.guardrail: Never clip consonants or remove every natural pause.

rules.rule: When the speaker makes a concrete claim, prefer owned or licensed visual proof over decorative stock.
rules.rationale: Evidence increases comprehension and trust.
rules.guardrail: If proof is unavailable, use a neutral editorial label rather than a fake screenshot.

rules.rule: Every B-roll request must state what the viewer should understand or feel, not only a search keyword.
rules.rationale: Intent enables better retrieval and prevents unrelated filler imagery.
rules.guardrail: Reject visuals that are topically similar but contradict the sentence.

rules.rule: Prefer inventory, item, map, location, player, health, crafting, combat, or before-after proof tied to the current state.
rules.rationale: Game-native evidence keeps narrative mechanics understandable.
rules.guardrail: Never generate gameplay-looking evidence for an event that was not captured.

rules.rule: Keep captions and labels clear of health, hotbar, crosshair, inventory, chat, and other essential HUD regions.
rules.rationale: The viewer must be able to read both the edit and game state.
rules.guardrail: Move or shorten text instead of covering critical HUD information.

rules.rule: Caption short meaning-complete phrases and highlight at most one or two consequential words.
rules.rationale: Phrase-level captions are readable and direct attention.
rules.guardrail: Do not turn every word into a competing animation.

rules.rule: For an editorial luxury look, use restrained white type, a single warm highlight color, generous spacing, and a subtle entrance.
rules.rationale: Hierarchy and restraint read as premium more reliably than constant motion.
rules.guardrail: Maintain contrast and mobile readability; style cannot obscure meaning.

rules.rule: Use a hard cut by default; earn stylized transitions through a real connection or major beat change.
rules.rationale: Unmotivated transitions slow pacing and advertise the edit.
rules.guardrail: Limit whips, glitches, and pushes when they do not preserve direction or meaning.

rules.rule: Use match cuts on shared motion, composition, item, location, or cause-effect relationships.
rules.rationale: A visual match can compress time while retaining orientation.
rules.guardrail: Do not label an arbitrary dissolve as a match cut.

rules.rule: Use silence, music withdrawal, risers, and impacts to shape contrast around major beats, not every cut.
rules.rationale: Sparse cues retain impact and guide emotion.
rules.guardrail: Dialogue intelligibility always wins; avoid repetitive or misleading impact sounds.

rules.rule: Each audio cue must identify its narrative purpose: anticipation, transition, reveal, impact, or relief.
rules.rationale: Purpose-based sound design is easier to review and less noisy.
rules.guardrail: Do not add an effect only because one exists in the asset pack.

rules.rule: Search in this order: exact owned asset, semantically matched owned asset, licensed library, honest original editorial graphic.
rules.rationale: The closest trustworthy source usually makes the strongest edit.
rules.guardrail: A generated graphic is not evidence and must retain generated provenance.

rules.rule: Generate only explanatory editorial forms such as title cards, stat layouts, player labels, item callouts, quote treatments, diagrams, or abstract backgrounds.
rules.rationale: Original graphics can clarify a beat without impersonating unavailable footage.
rules.guardrail: Never generate fake gameplay, UI screenshots, logos, people, quotes, proof, or branded assets that imply authenticity.

rules.rule: Use logos only when supplied by the user or clearly licensed; otherwise render the name as neutral text.
rules.rationale: A textual label can communicate identity without inventing brand artwork.
rules.guardrail: Do not redraw or hallucinate a third-party logo.

rules.rule: Preserve screen direction, spatial orientation, and action continuity unless disorientation is intentional and brief.
rules.rationale: Orientation lets viewers follow fast edits without cognitive reset.
rules.guardrail: Use an establishing frame or label after large location jumps.

rules.rule: Reject plans that stack caption emphasis, B-roll, zoom, transition, and SFX on the same ordinary word.
rules.rationale: Effect density should peak with narrative importance.
rules.guardrail: Ordinary connective speech should remain visually quiet.

rules.rule: A narrative plan with a hook must identify a supported reveal or payoff, or explicitly label the clip as an open loop.
rules.rationale: Unresolved promises damage retention and trust.
rules.guardrail: Do not invent a payoff to satisfy the rubric.
